title: Gene Coy's Black Aces: a Lubbock remark and no pay
summary: He joins Gene Coy through Lester Taylor, laughs at a white man's remark about the band's colour at a Lubbock dance, and leaves because Coy barely pays.

bands.name: Gene Coy and His Black Aces

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But getting back to Albuquerque, I met a guy... Also, we had a tenor player, another saxophone player named Lester Taylor. He said he could get me a gig with Gene Coy's band, so...

Yeah. So I said... Boy, I got to tell you about that. We played a dance... After I got with the band, we were playing a dance out in Lubbock, Texas. And so some White guy walks up to the band, and it said, "Gene Coy and His Black Aces." He looked up at it, and we had some dark fellows in the band, so the guy says, "Yup, they're plenty dark all right" -- they're plenty Black all right; that's what he really meant. So anyway, I mean, I laughed; I shouldn't have laughed, I guess. And all the guys turned around and looked at me. I said, "Well, I can't help it if you're Black. If you're black, you're Black." But anyway, that was... Oh, I cracked up behind that shit, because I really didn't expect nobody to say nothin' like that, and this cat just come up and looked at 'em, and said, "Yup, you're plenty Black all right." Oh boy, I thought that was funny, but the guys didn't think it was funny. So I learned a lesson from that, never to do that no more, don't laugh about being Black.

So anyway, I was with Gene Coy, and he was coming back through Albuquerque. But Gene Coy didn't pay nobody, you know what I mean? Like, we'd go play and play and play and play and play, and man, he'd wind up probably giving you two dollars or something. I said, "Gee, man, this ain't it."
You could do better on your own.

I was doing better out there in Albuquerque than I was being with this band. So Lester didn't join the band. He went on to Kansas, to Wichita, Kansas, and he told him about me, and he sent for me, and I joined the band like a dummy. I didn't know that I was supposed to get a salary. He didn't give me nothin' me, man. He gave me two dollars maybe every now and then. And then I had to buy my own food and everything, and it was just... It was horrible. I mean, what kind of job is this, where you work and you don't get paid? But anyway, he said he was going to Albuquerque, so I figured I'd wait til I get to Albuquerque and go back with the band that I was with before -- which I did.
